title: HPR001
extract_protocol_ch1: Single-cell suspensions were prepared from peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples following standard dissociation and filtration protocols to obtain high-quality, viable cells. Cell viability was confirmed to be greater than 85% using trypan blue exclusion. The concentration of each sample was adjusted to approximately 1,500–2,000 cells/µL to achieve the recommended target of up to 5,000 cells per sample for on-chip multiplexing using the 10x Genomics Chromium platform. Prior to loading, samples were inspected under a microscope to ensure the absence of debris and cell aggregates.

Following the recovery of the Gel Beads-In-Emulsions, the emulsions were broken, and barcoded complementary deoxyribonucleic acid was purified and amplified using the 10x Genomics GEM-X Universal Library Construction Kit. For on-chip multiplexing, each reaction was limited to approximately 5,000 cells per sample, ensuring comparable cell input and ribonucleic acid content across all multiplexed samples. Libraries were dual-indexed, pooled, and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 2000. Sequencing depth was adjusted to achieve approximately 20,000 reads per cell, depending on experimental design and transcriptome complexity.
data_processing: The demultiplexing, barcoded processing, gene counting and aggregation were made using the Cell Ranger software v3.0.2.
Assembly: GRCh38
Supplementary files format and content: Tab-separated values files and matrix files compressed with gzip
Supplementary files format and content: Integrated Seurat object
